countries.name: Argentina
countries.headline: Argentina keeps its Bienes Personales tax, with rates falling under Milei's 2024 reform
countries.summary: Argentina's personal assets tax (Bienes Personales) still applies to net wealth above an inflation-indexed minimum. The 2024 reform phases rates down through 2027, and the 1.25% bracket has gone. Taxpayers who complied on time get lower rates. For the 2025 fiscal year, filed in 2026, the general minimum was about ARS 384.7m.

countries.name: Australia
countries.headline: Greens keep a billionaire wealth tax on the table as Labor targets property and super tax breaks instead
countries.summary: Australia has no wealth tax. The Greens, whose votes the government often needs in the Senate, took a billionaire tax to the May 2025 election. The Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO) costed a 5% annual tax on net wealth between A$100m and A$1bn and 10% above A$1bn. The Greens said an earlier 10% version would raise A$23bn over four years and about A$50bn over a decade. Labor has not adopted it. Instead, Parliament passed higher tax on earnings from super balances above A$3m from July 2026. On 26 June 2026 Parliament passed Labor's law replacing the 50% capital gains discount with indexation and a 30% minimum tax from July 2027, and limiting negative gearing to new homes. In October 2026 the Greens said they would seek a Senate inquiry into Labor's weakened reform of discretionary trusts.

countries.name: Austria
countries.headline: Austria's SPÖ wants a millionaires' tax, but the coalition's 2027–28 budget rules out wealth taxes
countries.summary: Austria abolished its net wealth tax in 1994. SPÖ leader and Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler wants a tax on net wealth above €1m, with a €1.5m allowance for the family home. The party says it would raise about €5bn a year. In February 2026 parliament rejected a Greens motion for inheritance and gift taxes on large estates. In April 2026 the ÖVP-SPÖ-NEOS coalition agreed a 2027–28 double budget with no wealth or inheritance tax.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.headline: Belgium doubled its securities-account tax and taxes capital gains, and wealth taxes now split its coalition
countries.summary: Belgium has no net wealth tax. It levies an annual tax on securities accounts with an average value above €1m. A programme law published on 1 June 2026 doubled the rate from 0.15% to 0.30% for reference periods ending on or after that date. A 10% tax on realised capital gains on financial assets applies to gains from 1 January 2026, under a law of 6 April 2026. In October 2026 talks on the next federal budget stalled, with Vooruit and Les Engagés pressing for wealthy people to contribute more.

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.headline: Large-fortunes tax survives after a legislative committee rejected Paz's repeal bill
countries.summary: Bolivia's Impuesto a las Grandes Fortunas, created in 2020, remains in force. It taxes individuals with net wealth above Bs 30m at 1.4%–2.4%. In November 2025 President Rodrigo Paz announced plans to repeal it along with three other taxes, saying it drove capital abroad. In February 2026 a Chamber of Deputies committee rejected the repeal bill, and the government said it would send a new one. The tax authority set 30 April 2026 for residents' 2025 returns and 29 May 2026 for non-residents.
countries.revenue: Bs 795m in total from 2020 to the end of 2024

countries.name: Brazil
countries.headline: Brazil's minimum 10% tax on top incomes is in force, while a large-fortunes tax bill waits in Congress
countries.summary: Brazil's constitution allows a tax on large fortunes, but it has never been regulated. In November 2025 the Supreme Federal Court (STF) ruled 8-1 that Congress has failed to act, but set no deadline. In February 2026 a Workers' Party (PT) deputy filed a bill for 1%–3% on net wealth above R$10m. Law 15,270, in force since 1 January 2026, created a minimum income tax rising to 10% on incomes above R$1.2m a year and a 10% withholding on large dividends. An April 2026 International Tax Observatory study estimated that a 2% minimum tax on the very richest could raise about R$30bn a year.

countries.name: Canada
countries.headline: NDP leader Avi Lewis pushes a 1–3% wealth tax as Ottawa prepares a 5 November budget
countries.summary: Canada has no wealth tax. Avi Lewis, elected leader of the federal New Democratic Party (NDP) on 29 March 2026, proposes 1% on net wealth above C$10m, 2% above C$50m and 3% above C$100m, which he says would raise about C$40bn a year. Prime Minister Carney's government shows no sign of backing it. Finance Minister Champagne will table Budget 2026 on 5 November. In British Columbia, the Green Party campaigned on a one-time tax of 5%–20% on fortunes above C$50m, then an annual 2%–5% tax. The BC Conservatives won the 24 October 2026 provincial election with a majority.

countries.name: Chile
countries.headline: Chile has no wealth tax, and the Kast government's 2026 plan cuts corporate and inheritance taxes
countries.summary: Chile has no net wealth tax, and earlier proposals for a tax on the super-rich did not pass. President Kast's April 2026 economic reconstruction bill goes in the opposite direction. It cuts corporate income tax from 27% to 23% and lowers inheritance tax. There is no live wealth-tax proposal from the government or a major party.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.headline: Colombia's wealth tax still applies, but new President De la Espriella has pledged to abolish it
countries.summary: Since Law 2277 of 2022, Colombia has had a permanent wealth tax on individuals with net worth of 72,000 tax value units (UVT) or more, at 0.5%–1.5%. The Constitutional Court struck down Petro's December 2025 emergency, which had widened the tax, in April 2026. A separate February 2026 emergency created a one-year wealth tax on companies worth 200,000 UVT or more. The court partly suspended it in April. In July 2026 the outgoing Petro government filed a bill to cut the threshold to 40,000 UVT, but the new government wants it shelved. President Abelardo de la Espriella, sworn in on 7 August 2026, promised to scrap the wealth tax through a tax reform that still needs Congress.
countries.revenue: About COP 776bn in the first half of 2026, 56% of the annual target (individuals)

countries.name: Denmark
countries.headline: Denmark's PM dropped her wealth-tax plan to form a government, and the new coalition is cutting taxes
countries.summary: Denmark abolished its net wealth tax in 1997. On 26 February 2026 Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen proposed bringing one back for fewer than 60,000 people, to raise about DKK 6bn a year, and called an election for 24 March. On 1 May she dropped the plan, saying there was no majority for it. Her new four-party coalition, which published its programme on 2 June 2026, plans to cut corporate tax from 22% to 19% and scrap the highest income-tax bracket. The Red-Green Alliance (Enhedslisten), which supports the government, still proposes 1% a year on fortunes above DKK 35m.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.headline: Ecuador has no wealth tax since its one-off 2022 pandemic-era contribution expired
countries.summary: Ecuador imposed a temporary contribution on individuals with net wealth of at least US$1m (US$2m for couples) under its 2021 post-pandemic fiscal law, payable for 2022. It was a one-off and has not been renewed. There is no live proposal to bring it back.

countries.name: Finland
countries.headline: Finland's Left Alliance puts a 1% millionaires' tax in its €9bn tax plan for after the April 2027 election
countries.summary: Finland abolished its net wealth tax in 2006. The opposition Left Alliance proposes a 1% yearly tax on net assets above €1m, not counting the owner's home. In August 2026 it put the tax into a €9bn package of tax rises for the next government, and puts its yield at about €1bn a year. A poll commissioned by the party found 75% support. Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's governing parties want the next round of budget repair to come mainly from spending cuts. The next general election is on 18 April 2027.

countries.name: France
countries.headline: France's 2027 budget has no wealth tax, MPs rejected Zucman again, and a holding-company levy is pending
countries.summary: France replaced its net wealth tax in 2018 with a real-estate wealth tax (IFI), which taxes property only. The National Assembly rejected the Zucman 2% minimum tax on fortunes above €100m on 31 October 2025. The 2026 finance law, adopted in February 2026, created a tax on luxury non-business assets held in family holding companies. In September 2026 the Socialists' counter-budget brought back the Zucman tax, and the Court of Audit floated a 0.5% tax on non-business wealth above €5m. The government's 2027 budget bill, presented on 1 October, contains no new wealth tax. On 8 October the Assembly's finance committee backed a 2% annual tax on investment securities held in family holdings, but the floor debate restarts from the government's text. On 16 October the Assembly rejected the Zucman tax again, 70–35, along with amendments to bring back the ISF. The vote on the budget's first part is set for 3 November.

countries.name: Germany
countries.headline: Germany's wealth tax is suspended, the Greens propose a billionaire tax, and inheritance tax goes to court
countries.summary: Germany has not levied its wealth tax since 1997. The Left's motion to reinstate it, at 1% above €1m rising to 12% above €1bn, was referred to the Bundestag finance committee in March 2026. In September 2026 the Greens proposed a billionaire tax starting at 2% above €500m. The AfD has moved to abolish the dormant wealth tax law. Reviving the wealth tax is not a project of the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition. On 12 October 2026 the Federal Constitutional Court began hearing challenges to inheritance tax. A second day on 13 October covers relief for business assets. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) says the party will push its 'FairErben' inheritance reform once the court rules.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.headline: Iceland abolished its wealth tax in 2006, and a temporary crisis-era version lapsed after 2014
countries.summary: Iceland abolished its net wealth tax in 2006. After the 2008 financial crisis it brought in a temporary wealth tax of 1.25% on net assets above ISK 90m for individuals, which ran from 2010 to 2014. The Social Democratic Alliance, which now leads the government, campaigned in 2021 for a 1.5% tax above ISK 200m. Neither the 2026 nor the 2027 budget proposal includes a wealth tax.

countries.name: India
countries.headline: India abolished its wealth tax in 2015, and campaigners now urge a 2–6% levy on the ultra-rich
countries.summary: India abolished its wealth tax in the 2015 budget, with effect from 2016, and replaced it with a higher income-tax surcharge on top earners. The February 2026 budget left income-tax rates unchanged, and the government has rejected calls to revive a wealth tax or add an inheritance tax. In April 2026 the Centre for Financial Accountability (CFA) and the Tax the Top campaign called for a 2%–6% wealth tax on about 1,688 people worth more than ₹1,000 crore. No government or major-party proposal exists.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.headline: Irish opposition parties' 2027 alternative budgets include wealth taxes, but the government has no plan
countries.summary: Ireland had a short-lived wealth tax in the 1970s and has none today. Ahead of Budget 2027, opposition parties' alternative budgets include wealth-related levies. People Before Profit proposes 'radical' wealth taxes, and Sinn Féin proposes a 3% solidarity tax on incomes above €100,000. The government has no wealth-tax plans.

countries.name: Italy
countries.headline: Italy taxes foreign assets, while a citizens' bill and the AVS push wealth taxes above €2m and €5.4m
countries.summary: Italy taxes foreign financial assets (IVAFE) and foreign property (IVIE) but has no general net wealth tax. In May 2026 a committee filed '1% Equo', a popular-initiative bill for a tax of 1% to 3.5% on net wealth above €2m, excluding the main home. Collection runs until 15 November 2026, and promoters say they have passed the 50,000 signatures needed to send it to Parliament. In October 2026 the Greens-Left Alliance (AVS) proposed a tax on net wealth above €5.4m for the 2027 election. Prime Minister Meloni's government rejects any wealth tax.

countries.name: Japan
countries.headline: Japan dropped its post-war wealth tax in the 1950s, and its 2026 reform targets top incomes instead
countries.summary: Japan introduced a net wealth tax in 1950 under the Shoup mission's tax reforms. It was dropped after about three years because it raised little and was hard to enforce. There is no current wealth-tax proposal. Instead, the 2026 tax reform, passed by the Diet on 31 March 2026, tightens a minimum tax on very high incomes from 2027. It halves the special deduction from ¥330m to ¥165m and raises the rate from 22.5% to 30%.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.headline: Kenya has no wealth tax, and its Finance Act 2026 added none despite civil-society calls
countries.summary: Kenya has never had a net wealth tax, and no government or party has proposed one. Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi has said in principle that Kenya should tax wealth more and income less. But the Finance Act 2026, signed on 23 June 2026, added no new taxes. Civil-society groups keep pushing. The Institute of Public Finance (IPF), in work with Oxfam, estimates a wealth tax on net assets above Sh129m could raise up to Sh129.5bn (about $1bn) a year. Oxfam's November 2025 report found the richest 1% hold 78% of Kenya's financial wealth. In September 2026 experts urged the state to build systems to track wealth first.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.headline: Liechtenstein taxes wealth through income tax, using an assumed 4% return
countries.summary: Liechtenstein does not levy a separate wealth tax. It assumes an individual's net wealth earns a standard 4% return (Sollertrag) and adds that amount to taxable income. Real estate, securities and other movable assets are included.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.headline: A PT deputy files a wealth-tax bill, and Sheinbaum is open to study but plans no reform
countries.summary: Mexico has no wealth tax. In March 2026 a Labour Party (PT) deputy proposed rates of 1.5%–3.5% on fortunes above MXN 100m, estimated to raise MXN 40–60bn a year. In April 2026 President Sheinbaum said a tax on large fortunes should be analysed but that no tax-raising reform is currently planned.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.headline: Dutch cabinet now wants a capital gains tax for most Box 3 investments from 2028, as the Senate waits
countries.summary: Under transitional rules, the Netherlands taxes savings and investments (Box 3) on an assumed return, with a refund if the actual return was lower. The lower house passed the Box 3 Actual Return Act on 12 February 2026, but the Senate postponed its vote on 30 June 2026. On 29 September 2026 the cabinet proposed amending the bill so that about 90% of Box 3 wealth that changes in value is taxed on realised capital gains from 2028, with other assets to follow in 2030. To pay for it, the cabinet would cut the tax-free allowance to €30,846 in 2027, which drew criticism in the lower house. The government aims to send the amendment by 2 November, and the Senate wants to decide before Christmas. On 13 October the Senate finance committee said it will wait for the lower house to handle the amendment before deciding on the bill.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.headline: Greens and Te Pāti Māori campaign on wealth taxes before the November 2026 election, but Labour says no
countries.summary: New Zealand has no wealth tax and no general capital gains tax. Ahead of the 7 November 2026 election, the Greens propose a 2.5% annual tax on net assets above NZ$10m per person (NZ$20m for a couple), excluding the family home. They say it would hit about the richest 0.3%. Te Pāti Māori proposes rates of 1.5% to 2.5% on net wealth above NZ$2m. Labour leader Chris Hipkins says Labour will not adopt the Greens' tax policies and is campaigning on a 28% capital gains tax on investment and commercial property instead. National, ACT and NZ First oppose new taxes of this kind.

countries.name: Norway
countries.headline: Norway's 2027 budget lifts the wealth-tax allowance to NOK 1.99m, while a commission urges a lower rate
countries.summary: Norway levies a combined municipal and state net wealth tax of 1.0% on net wealth above NOK 1.9m in 2026, rising to 1.1% above NOK 21.5m. The 2026 budget raised the allowance from NOK 1.76m and made a deferred-payment scheme permanent. In June 2026 the Tax Commission (NOU 2026:9) proposed a single rate of 0.25% to 0.75%, a NOK 2m allowance and an end to valuation discounts on shares and homes. The 2027 budget proposal of 7 October 2026 raises the allowance to NOK 1.99m and keeps the rates. The government plans a white paper on wider tax reform in 2027.
countries.revenue: About NOK 34bn expected in 2025 (Ministry of Finance estimate)

countries.name: Peru
countries.headline: Peru has no wealth tax, and a fringe candidate's 2026 campaign pitch has not become a live proposal
countries.summary: Peru has no general personal wealth tax, though several bills since 2020 have proposed one. In the 30 March 2026 presidential debate, candidate Ronald Atencio proposed a tax on large fortunes to fund education. No government or parliamentary proposal has followed.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.headline: Portugal levies AIMI on high-value homes, and Livre wants a Zucman-style tax in the 2027 budget
countries.summary: Portugal has no net wealth tax. Its Adicional ao IMI (AIMI) is an annual surcharge on the combined taxable value of residential property, above €600,000 per individual (€1.2m for couples filing jointly). Rates run from 0.7% to 1.5%. The government delivered its 2027 budget bill on 8 October 2026 without a wealth tax. The left-wing party Livre says it will propose a surtax on fortunes above €100m during the budget debate. The final vote is due on 24 November.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.headline: South Africa's Treasury keeps rejecting a wealth tax despite opposition and budget-office calls
countries.summary: South Africa has no net wealth tax. It taxes wealth through estate duty, donations tax, securities transfer tax and transfer duty, which together raised R21.3bn in 2024/25, about 1.15% of tax revenue. Cabinet reportedly discussed a wealth tax during the 2025 budget impasse, and the Parliamentary Budget Office said one could raise about R38bn. In March 2026 Treasury told Parliament a wealth tax would add complexity and raise too little. In a July 2026 written reply to an Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) MP, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said the government is not considering one. Opposition parties, including the EFF and the MK Party, keep pressing for it.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.headline: South Korea plans to base its property holding tax on home values, raising the burden on investors
countries.summary: South Korea has no net wealth tax, but its comprehensive real estate holding tax is an annual levy on the combined value of a person's property above a threshold. An August 2026 government reform plan would base the tax more on home values and owner occupancy. It raises the deduction for single-home owners who live in their home to 1.4bn won and lifts the share of value that is taxed from 60% to 70%. The government expects about 2.18tn won (about $1.5bn) of extra revenue over five years. In September the ruling party and government settled the deduction for owners who do not live in their single home.

countries.name: Spain
countries.headline: Spain has a regional wealth tax and a permanent 'solidarity' tax above €3m, and Sumar seeks 3% above €50m
countries.summary: Spain has a regional net wealth tax. It also has a national Solidarity Tax on Large Fortunes (ISGF) on net wealth above €3m, at 1.7%–3.5%, which has been extended indefinitely. Revenue from the ISGF fell sharply after regions such as Madrid and Andalusia reinstated their own wealth tax, because regional tax paid is credited against it. Provisional Finance Ministry figures show about €2.5bn due on 2025 wealth tax returns. In September 2026 Sumar, the junior coalition partner, registered a bill in Congress for a 3% levy on fortunes above €50m to fund a universal child-rearing benefit. An October 2026 Work Inequality Lab study estimated the ISGF recouped about €500m of Madrid's wealth tax rebates.
countries.revenue: ~€2.51bn due on 2025 wealth tax returns (provisional, Finance Ministry, July 2026)

countries.name: Sweden
countries.headline: Sweden's left bloc won in September 2026 but has no government yet, and its biggest party rejects a wealth tax
countries.summary: Sweden abolished its wealth tax in 2007. The Left Party wants an inquiry into a tax on fortunes above SEK 1bn, which it says would cover about 540 people. The Greens want a billionaire tax based on Gabriel Zucman's plan. Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson rejects a wealth tax and called the claimed SEK 50bn in revenue a fantasy figure. The four opposition parties won 176 of 349 seats on 13 September 2026. Andersson handed back her first mandate to form a government on 28 September, after the Left Party backed the Moderate candidate for Speaker. The Speaker gave her a second mandate from 5 October. Andersson lost a Riksdag vote on 15 October, and Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist handed back a second attempt on 26 October. Ulf Kristersson stays on as caretaker prime minister.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.headline: Swiss cantons keep wealth taxes, voters reject a 50% inheritance tax and Vaud approves a 12% tax cut
countries.summary: All Swiss cantons levy a net wealth tax, with rates and allowances that vary widely between them. On 30 November 2025 about 78% of voters rejected the Young Socialists' (JUSO) initiative for a 50% federal tax on estates above CHF 50m. In September 2026 Vaud voters approved a 12% cut in cantonal income and wealth tax from 2027, and several central cantons are also cutting rates.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.headline: UK has no wealth tax, but Labour MPs and Greens press new Chancellor Healey before his 28 Oct budget
countries.summary: The UK has no annual wealth tax. The November 2025 budget introduced a High Value Council Tax surcharge on homes worth £2m or more in England from April 2028. Andy Burnham replaced Keir Starmer as Prime Minister in July 2026 and on 20 July named John Healey as Chancellor, replacing Rachel Reeves. Healey's first budget is due on 28 October 2026. A number of Labour MPs and campaigners back a 2% annual levy on assets above £10m, but analysts doubt the budget will include one. The Green Party under Zack Polanski proposes 1% a year on assets above £10m and 2% above £1bn.

countries.name: United States
countries.headline: California votes on 3 November on a one-time 5% billionaire tax, which now trails in the polls
countries.summary: There is no federal wealth tax. Bills from Sen. Warren (2% a year above $50m), Sen. Sanders and Rep. Khanna (5% a year on billionaires) and Sen. Wyden (annual tax on billionaires' gains) sit in committee with no chance of passing this Congress. California's Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' net worth, is on the 3 November 2026 ballot. It led in September polls, but an October PPIC poll found 46% yes and 52% no, with rival Prop 42 at 51%. If Prop 41 or 42 gets more votes than Prop 40, the billionaire tax dies. Opponents have raised about $187m against roughly $31m for supporters. Washington enacted a 9.9% tax on income above $1m, and repeal Initiative 645 is on the same ballot. Oregon unions filed a wealth-tax initiative for 2028. New York's tax on luxury second homes faces two court challenges.
countries.rate: California Prop 40: one-time 5% of net worth (proposed)
countries.threshold: California Prop 40: net worth of $1bn or more, residents on 1 January 2026
countries.revenue: California Prop 40: tens of billions of dollars spread over several years from 2027 (Legislative Analyst's Office estimate)

countries.name: Uruguay
countries.headline: Uruguay keeps its wealth tax, and the government rules out unions' 1% surcharge on the richest for now
countries.summary: Uruguay levies a net wealth tax (Impuesto al Patrimonio) on individuals above an indexed minimum, set at UYU 6.653m for 2025. In November 2025 the PIT-CNT union federation proposed a 1% surcharge on about 25,000 people with more than US$1m. President Orsi said he would study it, but the Economy Minister has repeatedly rejected it. In September 2026 the government ruled out short-term tax changes.

items.title: PPIC poll: support for California's billionaire tax falls to 46%, behind a rival measure
items.summary: Likely voters split 46% yes and 52% no (16–22 October), down from 52% support in September. Prop 42, which would ban wealth taxes, polled 51% and Prop 41 was tied.

items.title: Study finds the solidarity tax recouped about €500m of Madrid's wealth tax rebates
items.summary: Work by the Piketty-linked Work Inequality Lab finds wealth and solidarity tax revenue rose 45% between 2021 and 2023, and proposes minimum taxation of wealth from €700,000.

items.title: Sweden still has no government after the Centre leader hands back her mandate
items.summary: Andersson lost a vote in the Riksdag on 15 October. Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist then found no majority for a centrist government. The Speaker can call a new vote or ask another leader to try.

items.title: BC Conservatives win a majority in the provincial election, ending nine years of NDP government
items.summary: The Greens, who campaigned on a tax on fortunes above C$50m, won at least two seats on election night.

items.title: Champagne sets 5 November for Budget 2026 as the budget officer warns deficits are deepening
items.summary: The Parliamentary Budget Officer says new spending adds about C$3bn a year to deficits compared with June and puts the 2030-31 deficit above C$63bn.

items.title: French National Assembly rejects the Zucman 2% minimum tax again, this time in the 2027 budget
items.summary: The plenary voted 70–35 against the left's amendment, a far smaller turnout than the 228–172 vote in October 2025. Socialist and ecologist versions and amendments to bring back the ISF also failed. The vote on the budget's first part was moved to 3 November.

items.title: Greens to seek a Senate inquiry into Labor's weakened tax reform for discretionary trusts
items.summary: The Greens say concessions have watered the plan down and they won't back a bill that doesn't make wealthy Australians pay their fair share. The bill had not yet reached Parliament.

items.title: Dutch Senate finance committee will wait for the amending bill before deciding on Box 3
items.summary: The committee provisionally agreed with the cabinet's route and will wait for the lower house to handle the amending bill. No Senate vote date is set.

items.title: German Constitutional Court hears challenges to inheritance tax rules
items.summary: Bavaria argues the federal rules on valuation, allowances and rates are unconstitutional. A second hearing on 13 October covers tax breaks for business assets. A ruling is expected within months.

items.title: Belgian budget talks stall as Vooruit and Les Engagés push for the wealthy to pay more
items.summary: Prime Minister Bart De Wever cancelled his 13 October State of the Union speech. Extra taxes on wealthy people are among the sticking points in finding at least €10bn.

items.title: Finance Minister Klingbeil says inheritance tax needs reform once the court rules
items.summary: He criticised that large fortunes are often passed on almost tax-free. The CDU/CSU opposes a higher inheritance tax.

items.title: Oregon unions file 'Financial Assets Tax on Multimillionaires' initiative for 2028 ballot
items.summary: A coalition including teachers' and public-sector unions filed a state wealth-tax initiative to offset federal benefit cuts and cut taxes for low earners.

items.title: French finance committee backs 2% annual tax on investment securities held in family holdings
items.summary: The amendment by Charles de Courson (LIOT group) passed in committee. The committee then rejected the whole revenue section on 9 October, so the floor debate restarts from the government's text.

items.title: Norway's 2027 budget proposal lifts wealth-tax allowance to NOK 1.99m, keeps rates
items.summary: Rates and the NOK 21.5m upper-bracket threshold are unchanged. Bigger reforms will wait for the Tax Commission's report, NOU 2026:9.

items.title: Newsom backs Prop 42 to cancel California billionaire tax and bar future wealth taxes
items.summary: Gov. Newsom endorsed a rival measure, funded by Sergey Brin, that would cancel Prop 40 and ban new taxes on personal property. This puts him at odds with parts of his party and labor.

items.title: BC Greens propose one-time 5%–20% tax on fortunes over C$50m ahead of provincial election
items.summary: Leader Emily Lowan's Fair Share Act would follow with an annual 2%–5% wealth tax. The party says it would raise C$22.2bn in year one and C$5.4bn a year after.

items.title: Bernie Sanders rallies for California's Prop 40 in San Francisco and Los Angeles
items.summary: Sanders called the billionaire tax the most important ballot measure in the country. Rep. Ro Khanna also spoke.

items.title: Five tax measures on California ballot, including billionaire tax Prop 40 and rivals 41 and 42
items.summary: An explainer on the competing measures. If more than one passes, the one with the most votes wins. Opponents are spending hundreds of millions.

items.title: Italy's Greens-Left Alliance proposes wealth tax on super-rich and tax cuts for 98%
items.summary: The Greens-Left Alliance (AVS) election plan would tax net wealth above €5.4m. AVS also challenges Schlein and Conte to back it.

items.title: Irish opposition alternative budgets propose wealth and windfall taxes for 2027
items.summary: Sinn Féin and other parties set out levies on high earners, banks and wealth ahead of Budget 2027.

items.title: French government presents 2027 budget bill with no new wealth tax
items.summary: The bill extends the 'differential contribution', a minimum 20% tax on very high incomes first levied in 2025. It does not include the Zucman tax.

items.title: NBC News poll puts California's billionaire tax at 48% yes, 38% no, short of a majority
items.summary: Another 14% of voters were undecided, leaving the outcome open five weeks before the vote.

items.title: New data put Uruguay's top 1% at about 40% of wealth, reviving the tax-the-rich debate
items.summary: A wealth-distribution indicator reignited calls for the PIT-CNT union federation's surcharge. The government has ruled out short-term tax changes.

items.title: Dutch cabinet proposes capital gains tax for most Box 3 investments from 2028
items.summary: A letter to parliament says about 90% of Box 3 wealth that changes in value would be taxed on gains from 2028, with the rest from 2030. The tax-free allowance would fall to €30,846 in 2027.

items.title: German Greens propose tax on fortunes above €500m starting at 2%
items.summary: The party says the levy would hit a few hundred people and raise about €20bn a year.

items.title: Judge orders New York City to redo the rollout of its tax on luxury second homes
items.summary: The state-enacted surcharge targets second homes worth $5m or more. A Staten Island judge ordered new notices to owners, and Florida residents Stephen Wynn and Wilbur Ross filed a separate suit calling the tax unconstitutional. The city will appeal.

items.title: Andersson hands back her mandate to form a Swedish government after the Left Party backs the Moderate Speaker
items.summary: The Speaker later gave her a second mandate starting on 5 October, with a report due around 12 October.

items.title: Vaud voters approve 12% cut in cantonal income and wealth tax
items.summary: Just over 53% backed the business-led initiative. The canton estimates it will lose about CHF 272m in revenue a year from 2027.

items.title: Korea settles property holding tax deduction and delays capital gains overhaul to November
items.summary: Officials agreed the deduction for single-home owners who do not live in their home. Capital gains changes move to a November tax subcommittee.

items.title: France's Court of Audit floats a 0.5% tax on non-business wealth above €5m
items.summary: A note on household wealth taxation proposed a 'differential tax on personal wealth', with real-estate wealth tax paid credited against it. The free-market iFRAP foundation, which opposes it, reports an estimated yield of €1.4bn.

items.title: Sweden's left bloc wins narrow majority, with wealth-tax supporters among its parties
items.summary: The Left Party and the Greens back a wealth tax, while Social Democrat leader Andersson has rejected one.

items.title: Sumar registers bill for a 3% tax on fortunes above €50m in Spanish Congress
items.summary: The bill would also end the family-business exemption and the joint income and wealth tax cap for these fortunes. Revenue would fund a universal child-rearing benefit.

items.title: French Socialists' 2027 counter-budget revives Zucman 2% minimum tax on fortunes over €100m
items.summary: The Socialist (PS) plan sets out €39.5bn of new revenue, with the Zucman tax as its centrepiece at an estimated €15bn. The plan is non-binding.

items.title: PPIC poll: 52% back California's billionaire tax, but rival Props 41 and 42 also win majorities
items.summary: The Public Policy Institute of California found 52% yes and 46% no on Prop 40 among likely voters. Prop 41 had 51% and Prop 42 had 54%. A Politico and UC Berkeley poll taken days later put Prop 40 at 45% yes and 43% no.

items.title: Calls grow for Kenya to tax wealth of the ultra-rich
items.summary: Experts urge building asset-tracking systems before adopting a net wealth tax.

items.title: Spotify co-founder Martin Lorentzon says he would leave Sweden at once if a wealth tax is brought in
items.summary: He said he backs progressive taxes but opposes a yearly levy on wealth, which could force founders to sell shares to pay it.

items.title: Social Democrat leader Andersson rejects the Left Party and Greens' billionaire-tax plans
items.summary: In an SVT interview she called the claimed SEK 50bn in revenue a fantasy figure and said her party has no billionaire-tax plan of its own.

items.title: Billionaire-funded group raises $187m to defeat California's billionaire tax through Props 41 and 42
items.summary: Sergey Brin and other billionaires fund the opposition. Supporters, mainly the SEIU-UHW health workers' union, have raised about $31m. The measure with the most votes wins.

items.title: Te Pāti Māori proposes a wealth tax of 1.5% to 2.5% on net wealth above NZ$2m
items.summary: Its 'Kiwi Tax Plan' also adds a 5% stamp duty on home sales and makes the first NZ$30,000 of income tax-free.

items.title: UN tax convention talks close their fifth session in New York, with draft texts for all three instruments
items.summary: Negotiators worked on the framework convention and two early protocols, on cross-border services and on tax disputes. The sixth session is in Nairobi from 30 November to 10 December 2026.
items.source: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs

items.title: New Colombian President De la Espriella pledges to abolish the wealth tax in his inaugural speech
items.summary: He said the country must stop punishing those who invest. Repeal needs a tax reform passed by Congress, which the finance minister said would come in the autumn.

items.title: South Korea plans to base its property holding tax on home values and owner occupancy
items.summary: The plan raises rates on expensive and rented homes and is expected to bring in about 2.18tn won more over five years.

items.title: Finland's Left Alliance includes a millionaires' tax in a €9bn tax package for the next government
items.summary: The package also removes dividend tax relief for unlisted companies. The party says the millionaires' tax would raise about €1bn a year.

items.title: Outgoing Petro government files tax bill to cut Colombia's wealth-tax threshold to 40,000 UVT
items.summary: The bill aims to raise COP 21.9tn in 2027 and would roughly triple the number of wealth-tax payers. The incoming finance minister said it should be shelved.

items.title: New Prime Minister Andy Burnham names John Healey as Chancellor
items.summary: Healey, a former defence secretary, replaced Rachel Reeves. His first budget is set for 28 October 2026.

items.title: Initiative 645 to repeal Washington's millionaires' tax qualifies for the November 2026 ballot
items.summary: Let's Go Washington, led by hedge-fund founder Brian Heywood, filed about 511,000 signatures. The tax on income above $1m is due to start in 2028.

items.title: Spain's Finance Ministry reports about €2.5bn due on 2025 wealth tax returns
items.summary: More than 227,800 wealth tax returns were filed in the 2026 campaign. The figures are provisional.

items.title: Finance minister tells Parliament South Africa is not considering a wealth tax
items.summary: Replying to EFF MP Carl Niehaus, Godongwana said existing wealth taxes raised R21.3bn in 2024/25 and that wealth taxes have failed in several countries.

items.title: Dutch Senate delays vote on Box 3 actual-return tax
items.summary: After a full debate, the upper house paused the bill while the government considers measures to soften it.

items.title: Newsom proposes national billionaires' minimum tax while opposing California's one-time levy
items.summary: The California governor called for a federal minimum tax on people worth over $100m, arguing the fight belongs at the federal level.

items.title: Parliament passes the law replacing the 50% capital gains discount with indexation
items.summary: The package adds a 30% minimum tax on capital gains and limits negative gearing to new housing. The capital gains changes apply to gains accruing from 1 July 2027.

items.title: Norway's Tax Commission proposes one lower wealth-tax rate of 0.25%–0.75% and an end to valuation discounts
items.summary: The report, NOU 2026:9, would raise the allowance to NOK 2m and add a separate allowance for the main home. Members did not agree on one rate. Public consultation closed on 24 September 2026.

items.title: Labour's Hipkins says he will not adopt the Greens' tax plans to form a government
items.summary: Hipkins said Labour disagrees with most of the Greens' package and will stick to its own capital gains tax on property.

items.title: Ruto signs Finance Act 2026, which adds no new taxes and no wealth tax
items.summary: The law funds the Sh4.8 trillion 2026/27 budget and focuses on compliance and closing loopholes rather than new taxes.

items.title: New Zealand Greens propose a 2.5% annual tax on net wealth above NZ$10m
items.summary: The scaled-back 'super-rich tax' replaces a NZ$2m threshold and comes with an inheritance and gifts tax and higher corporate rates.

items.title: California one-time 5% billionaire tax qualifies for the November 2026 ballot
items.summary: The Secretary of State confirmed enough valid signatures. The measure taxes the net worth of billionaires living in the state on 1 January 2026, payable over five years.

items.title: Denmark's new Frederiksen-led coalition plans corporate and income-tax cuts, with no wealth tax
items.summary: The programme cuts corporate tax from 22% to 19% over three years and scraps the highest income-tax bracket.

items.title: Belgium doubles securities-account tax to 0.30% on accounts above €1m
items.summary: The programme law applies the higher rate to reference periods ending from 1 June 2026.

items.title: Activists urge Kenyan MPs to rework the Finance Bill to tax the rich, citing up to Sh129.5bn a year
items.summary: The Institute of Public Finance proposed a wealth tax on net assets above Sh129m. Treasury said the bill raises no tax rates.

items.title: Popular-initiative bill for Italian wealth tax above €2m launches signature drive
items.summary: The '1% Equo' bill would tax net wealth above €2m at 1% to 3.5%, excluding the main home, and raise inheritance tax. It needs 50,000 signatures by 15 November 2026.

items.title: Australia's 2026 budget breaks an election promise to curb capital gains and negative gearing breaks
items.summary: The 50% capital gains discount would give way to indexation and a 30% minimum tax from July 2027. Negative gearing is limited to new homes.

items.title: Washington Supreme Court blocks referendum on the new 9.9% millionaires' income tax
items.summary: The court ruled unanimously that the law supports state government and so is exempt from a referendum. It did not rule on whether the tax is constitutional.

items.title: Danish PM Frederiksen drops wealth tax to ease government talks
items.summary: She said there was no parliamentary majority for the levy proposed before the March election.

items.title: With Austria's budget in deficit, the SPÖ and unions renew their call for a millionaires' tax
items.summary: Vice-Chancellor Babler's model would tax net wealth above €1m. Coalition partners oppose it.

items.title: Colombian court suspends second instalment of the corporate wealth tax for non-profits
items.summary: The 6-3 ruling covers non-profit bodies and companies in liquidation until the court decides on the decree in full.

items.title: Austria's coalition agrees 2027–28 budget with no wealth or inheritance tax
items.summary: Chancellor Stocker said there would be no wealth or inheritance tax and no property tax rise. The plan instead extends the bank levy and raises some corporate and property-gains taxes.

items.title: Bundestag debates AfD motion to repeal dormant wealth tax law
items.summary: The motion to abolish the Wealth Tax Act (Vermögensteuergesetz) was sent to committees.

items.title: Chile's Kast sends tax package cutting corporate and inheritance taxes
items.summary: The reconstruction bill lowers the corporate rate from 27% to 23% and eases inheritance tax. Critics say it favours the richest.

items.title: Spain and Brazil agree to sign a memorandum on taxing the super-rich at their Barcelona meeting
items.summary: Finance ministers Arcadi España and Dario Durigan met during the democracy summit in Barcelona. Gabriel Zucman presented his plan for a minimum tax of at least 2% a year on the very rich.

items.title: Sánchez and Lula rally progressive leaders in Barcelona, with taxing the super-rich on the agenda
items.summary: The 'In Defense of Democracy' gathering followed the first Spain-Brazil summit.

items.title: Study estimates a 2% minimum tax on large Brazilian fortunes could raise R$30bn a year
items.summary: The International Tax Observatory study, with a preface by the Finance Ministry, targets about 1,430 people worth over R$500m.

items.title: Sheinbaum says a tax on large fortunes should be analysed, but no reform is planned
items.summary: The Mexican president defended the progressive income tax and opened the door to future study.

items.title: Oxfam finds only 3% of IMF tax advice to governments targets wealth or income from wealth
items.summary: Of 1,049 tax recommendations to 125 countries in 2022–2024, just 30 dealt with net wealth taxes or taxing income from wealth. Released before the IMF Spring Meetings.

items.title: Colombia's Constitutional Court strikes down Petro's economic emergency
items.summary: The ruling struck down the emergency under which the wealth-tax threshold had been cut and rates raised by decree.

items.title: Indian report urges 2%–6% wealth tax on 1,688 ultra-rich individuals
items.summary: The Wealth Tracker India 2026 by CFA and Tax the Top says this tax, plus an inheritance tax, could fund about ₹10.6 lakh crore a year of welfare.

items.title: Japan's Diet passes 2026 tax reform, tightening a minimum tax on ultra-high incomes from 2027
items.summary: The reform lowers the deduction under the high-income minimum tax from ¥330m to ¥165m and raises its rate from 22.5% to 30%. It is not a wealth tax.

items.title: Washington enacts 9.9% 'millionaires' tax' on income over $1m, but wealth tax bills stall
items.summary: SB 6346 takes effect in 2028. Separate bills for a tax on financial intangible assets stayed in committee when the 2026 session ended.

items.title: Peruvian presidential candidate proposes tax on large fortunes in debate
items.summary: Ronald Atencio pitched a wealth tax with other measures to fund education.

items.title: Avi Lewis wins NDP leadership on platform including wealth tax on richest 1%
items.summary: Lewis estimates his wealth tax would raise about C$40bn a year.

items.title: Warren, Jayapal and Boyle reintroduce Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act with 45+ lawmakers
items.summary: The bill would levy 2% a year on net worth over $50m plus a surcharge on billionaires. Saez and Zucman estimate it would raise about $6.2tn over ten years.

items.title: Treasury rejects renewed wealth-tax calls at Parliament's 2026 budget hearings
items.summary: Treasury's Chris Axelson said a dedicated wealth tax would add administrative complexity and might not raise enough to justify its costs.

items.title: Parliament passes higher tax on earnings from super balances above A$3m, from July 2026
items.summary: The total rate rises to 30% on earnings linked to balances above A$3m and 40% above A$10m. Unrealised gains are excluded.

items.title: Argentina's personal assets tax has higher minimums and lower rates for 2026 filings
items.summary: Thresholds were indexed about 31% for inflation and the top 1.25% bracket disappears as rates step down toward 2027.

items.title: Left Party motion to reinstate German wealth tax sent to finance committee
items.summary: The motion proposes 1% above €1m rising to 5% at €50m and 12% above €1bn.

items.title: Mexican PT deputy proposes 1.5%–3.5% wealth tax on fortunes above MXN 100m
items.summary: The initiative aims to raise MXN 40–60bn a year to reduce poverty.

items.title: Sanders and Khanna introduce a 5% annual wealth tax on America's 938 billionaires
items.summary: The Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act would raise an estimated $4.4tn. It was referred to the Senate Finance Committee.

items.title: Danish PM proposes reinstating wealth tax as she calls snap election
items.summary: Frederiksen's plan, expected to raise about $1bn, would hit fewer than 60,000 people.

items.title: Austrian parliament rejects Greens' motion for inheritance and gift taxes on large estates
items.summary: No other group backed it. ÖVP and NEOS said such taxes would make business handovers and saving harder.

items.title: France's 2026 finance law creates tax on luxury assets held in family holding companies
items.summary: The law was adopted on 2 February using Article 49.3, and the Constitutional Council largely upheld it. The levy targets non-business assets in holdings worth over €5m.

items.title: Dutch lower house passes Box 3 reform taxing actual investment returns from 2028
items.summary: The bill replaces deemed returns on savings and investments with taxation of real returns.

items.title: Bolivian deputies' committee rejects bill to abolish large-fortunes tax
items.summary: The planning committee kept the wealth tax while approving repeal of the financial transactions tax. The committee chair said the government must send a new bill.

items.title: PT deputy files bill for a 1%–3% tax on Brazilian fortunes above R$10m
items.summary: Bill PLP 5/2026 by Pedro Uczai would send all revenue to the anti-poverty fund. It has not advanced.

items.title: Colombia's second emergency creates a one-year wealth tax on companies worth 200,000 UVT or more
items.summary: Decree 173, issued under the February 2026 emergency for climate disasters, applies to companies for 2026. The first instalment was due on 1 April.

items.title: Colombian court provisionally suspends emergency decree and its new taxes
items.summary: The court voted 6-2 to suspend the emergency, including the decree widening the wealth tax to holdings above 40,000 tax value units (UVT).

items.title: Oxfam says billionaire wealth hit a record $18.3tn in 2025 and calls for taxes on extreme wealth
items.summary: Released as Davos opened, the 'Resisting the Rule of the Rich' report urges higher taxes on the richest.

items.title: SPD unveils 'FairErben' inheritance tax concept with €1m lifetime allowance
items.summary: The paper would sharply limit business-asset exemptions. It is a discussion paper, not a bill.

items.title: Belgium introduces 10% tax on capital gains from financial assets
items.summary: The law of 6 April 2026 taxes gains realised from 1 January 2026 at 10% above an indexed €10,000 annual exemption. Gains built up before 2026 are exempt.

items.title: EU Tax Observatory study says past European wealth taxes failed through narrow bases, not mainly flight
items.summary: The study for the Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung urges broad bases, high thresholds, minimum-tax top-ups and anti-exile rules. It was presented in Brussels on 11 December 2025.

items.title: Colombian Congress sinks Petro's 2026 financing tax reform
items.summary: Economic committees voted 9-4 against the bill, and the government then turned to emergency decrees.

items.title: Norway's 2026 budget raises wealth-tax allowance and makes deferral scheme permanent
items.summary: The basic allowance rose from NOK 1.76m to NOK 1.9m and the low-valuation limit for homes rose to NOK 14m.

items.title: Godongwana doubles down that a wealth tax is not viable for South Africa
items.summary: The finance minister said South Africa already taxes the wealthy as heavily as many rich countries. Treasury warned emigration could cost up to R49bn a year.

items.title: Institute of Public Finance and Oxfam ask whether Kenya can get wealth taxation right
items.summary: The report finds Kenya lacks an enforceable framework for taxing the wealthy and sets out what must be fixed for a wealth tax to work.

items.title: World Inequality Report 2026 backs a global minimum tax on billionaires and centimillionaires
items.summary: The World Inequality Lab finds fewer than 60,000 people, the top 0.001%, own three times the wealth of the poorest half of humanity.

items.title: Swiss voters reject JUSO initiative for 50% tax on inheritances over CHF 50m
items.summary: About 78% voted no and no canton approved it. The proceeds would have funded climate measures.

items.title: UK budget adds surcharge on homes worth £2m+ instead of a wealth tax
items.summary: The High Value Council Tax charge starts in April 2028, alongside higher tax rates on dividends and property income.

items.title: Oxfam says Kenya's 125 richest people hold more wealth than 42.6 million citizens
items.summary: The report also found the richest 1% hold 78% of financial wealth and called Kenya's tax system regressive.

items.title: Lula signs law creating minimum 10% tax on Brazil's top incomes
items.summary: Law 15,270 exempts earnings up to R$5,000 a month and imposes a minimum rate on incomes above R$600k, reaching 10% above R$1.2m, from 2026.

items.title: Bolivian President Paz moves to scrap large-fortunes tax to attract investment
items.summary: Paz announced repeal of four taxes, arguing the 2020 wealth tax drove investment abroad.

items.title: G20 Johannesburg summit ends without progress on taxing the super-rich, says Greenpeace
items.summary: Advocates praised South Africa's leadership but said no new commitments followed the 2024 Rio pledge.

items.title: UN tax convention talks resume in Nairobi with focus on high-net-worth individuals
items.summary: The third negotiating session debated an article on taxing wealthy individuals alongside allocation of taxing rights.

items.title: Brazil's Supreme Court rules Congress has failed to create the constitutional tax on large fortunes
items.summary: The court ruled 8-1 in a case brought by the PSOL party in 2019, but set no deadline for Congress to act.

items.title: Uruguayan unions propose 1% surcharge on wealth of the richest 1%
items.summary: The PIT-CNT plan would hit about 25,000 people with over US$1m and fund households with children.

items.title: French National Assembly rejects Zucman tax and Socialist alternative in 2026 budget debate
items.summary: Lawmakers voted down the 2% levy on wealth above €100m and a 3% levy above €10m. The government offered a holding-company tax instead.

items.title: Illinois House Democrats float 4.95% tax on billionaires' unrealized gains to fund transit
items.summary: The plan was dropped from the final transit bill two days later after Gov. Pritzker opposed new revenue of this kind.

items.title: Union-backed one-time billionaire tax initiative filed in California
items.summary: SEIU-UHW's proposal would impose a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' wealth to fund health care after federal cuts.

items.title: Wyden reintroduces Billionaires Income Tax Act to tax billionaires' gains every year
items.summary: The bill (S.2845) would end deferral strategies such as 'buy, borrow, die'. It sits in the Senate Finance Committee.

items.title: Norway's Labour Party wins re-election after a campaign where the wealth tax was a central issue
items.summary: Labour defended the tax, the Conservatives wanted it cut and the Progress Party wanted it scrapped. Labour put the cost of abolishing it at NOK 34bn a year.

items.title: Spain and Brazil launch a push to tax the super-rich at FfD4 in Seville, with South Africa joining
items.summary: The initiative sits under the Sevilla Platform for Action and invites more countries to join. Spain's release names Spain and Brazil. Oxfam said South Africa had joined.

items.title: Budget office costs Greens' tax of 5% on wealth over A$100m and 10% over A$1bn
items.summary: The Parliamentary Budget Office said the behavioural response of the very rich to the tax is highly uncertain.

items.title: Greens announce a 10% annual tax on the net wealth of Australia's roughly 150 billionaires
items.summary: The party said the tax would raise A$23bn over four years and fund dental care in Medicare and free GP visits. Labor did not back it.
